subject: Architecture
title: The Rana Plaza Factory Collapse
description: One-minute skill: The Rana Plaza Factory Collapse.

hook.text: In 2013, a garment factory in Bangladesh collapsed, killing 1,134 workers — the deadliest structural failure in history.

buildup.text: Rana Plaza was an eight-story commercial building with three illegally added floors housing garment factories.

discovery.text: Large cracks appeared the day before. An engineer condemned the building. The owner ordered workers back inside.

twist.text: The factories supplied major Western fashion brands. Global consumers were unknowingly connected to the tragedy.

climax.text: The disaster sparked the global Fashion Revolution movement — 'Who made my clothes?' became a rallying cry.

punchline.text: 1,134 people died making clothes. The world asked who paid.

quiz.question: What movement did the Rana Plaza collapse inspire?
options: The Fair Trade certification for clothing

details.summary: Rana Plaza in Dhaka, Bangladesh, collapsed on April 24, 2013, killing 1,134 garment workers in the fashion industry's deadliest disaster. The eight-story building was constructed with substandard materials on swampy ground, and workers were ordered inside despite visible cracks the day before.
details.whyItMatters: Rana Plaza connected architectural failure to global supply chains. It forced the fashion industry to confront how cost-cutting in construction and safety directly threatens the lives of workers producing clothes for Western consumers.
takeaways: Rana Plaza collapsed in 2013, killing 1,134 garment workers
Substandard construction and ignored warnings caused the disaster
It forced the fashion industry to address factory safety

faq.question: Why did Rana Plaza collapse?
faq.answer: The building was constructed on filled-in swampland with substandard concrete and rebar. Three upper floors were added without permits. Heavy vibrations from garment factory generators stressed weak columns. Workers reported cracks the day before but were ordered to return to work.

faq.question: What changed after Rana Plaza?
faq.answer: The Accord on Fire and Building Safety in Bangladesh was signed by over 200 brands, establishing independent safety inspections of garment factories. Over 1,600 factories were inspected and remediated.
